facts.text: Slade Craven is played by John Mann, frontman of Canadian folk-rockers Spirit of the West, whose drinking song "Home for a Rest" is called Canada's unofficial national anthem.
This was Trimark Pictures' last released movie. The studio had cranked out the Turbulence series as direct-to-video thrillers.
Craig Sheffer led both Turbulence 2 and this one, but plays a different character each time. Continuity was not this franchise's thing.
Director Jorge Montesi was mostly a TV director, with credits like Andromeda, Mutant X, Relic Hunter and Queen of Swords.
Monika Schnarre won the Ford Supermodel of the World contest at 14, and at 15 was the youngest ever in the Sports Illustrated swimsuit issue.
Gabrielle Anwar once held a record as the World's Fastest Talker, set at a Guinness exhibit in London while still at drama school.
The tagline promised: One killer. Forty hostages. Ten million internet viewers. Webcast concerts were very much a 2001 fantasy.
Filmed in Vancouver, British Columbia, where the 747 airport scenes were cast as Los Angeles.
Rutger Hauer and John Mann died four months apart in 2019: Hauer on July 19, Mann on November 20.
One critic said Rutger Hauer flies the plane, sighs occasionally and listens to classical music, and you can see the wry amusement in his body language.
Screenwriter Wade Ferley reportedly has more credits in camera and electrical departments than for writing.
Red Letter Media crowned this the winner of a Best of the Worst episode (Plinketto #4) for being the most entertaining of the bunch.
Joe Mantegna later played an FBI agent on Criminal Minds from 2007 to 2020, a longer FBI tour than here.
Reviewer Nathan Rabin called it a bootleg Passenger 57 with a knock-off Marilyn Manson fighting an off-brand evil Marilyn Manson.
John Mann survived colorectal cancer around 2010, then was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's in September 2014. His story inspired benefit concerts and the documentary Spirit Unforgettable.
Released May 2001, this was a final flight of the Turbulence trilogy, which started with the 1997 theatrical hit starring Ray Liotta.
